description: CIRFI (Critical Infrastructure Resilience Failure Indicators) is a research project and online tool of the Faculty of Safety Engineering at VŠB – Technical University of Ostrava, with Tomas Bata University in Zlín, the University of Žilina and Brno University of Technology, funded by the Czech Ministry of the Interior security research programme from 2020 to 2022. It set out to determine indicators of resilience failure for subsystems (sectors, subsectors and elements) of technical critical infrastructure, namely energy, transport and information and communication technologies, and to build a tool that identifies these indicators and assesses their suitability for specific subsystems. The project builds on earlier work on assessing the resilience of critical infrastructure elements and their cascading and synergic impacts. The web-based CIRFI Tool walks the user through steps: selecting and characterising the infrastructure element of interest (linear, point or area element), with multi-criteria or pairwise comparison methods suggested for the selection, and then identifying resilience failure indicators. Access to the tool is free online; no licence is stated. Caveats: the tool is in Czech and the project ended in 2022. Coverage is the Czech Republic, with a general method. It supports resilience and cascading failure analysis of energy, transport and ICT infrastructure, such as building vulnerability maps for operators and authorities; there are no related records in the catalogue yet.
